headline: High: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP while Plane ingests files and hyperlinks, creating default-path prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, and its shared state is via filesystem; Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Plane content is copied into the workspace or MCP-fed, but the pair lacks a documented direct channel, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Plane content is copied into a shared workspace file that Continue reads
IF an MCP server forwards Plane text into Continue prompts without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable MCP servers not needed for this workflow
Keep Plane exports outside the IDE workspace
Use a read-only staging folder for imported files
Add a manual review step before any pasted task text is treated as instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and can write/read workspace files; Plane handles files, notes, issues, and hyperlinks. If both are used on the same workspace, sensitive code or notes can flow from Continue into Plane uploads or task content, so leakage is plausible in default collaboration patterns.
conditions: IF the same repository or notes folder is shared between the IDE and Plane
IF a user uploads workspace files from Continue into Plane
mitigations: Separate Plane attachments from the coding workspace
Redact secrets before uploading files to Plane
Restrict Continue to a non-sensitive project when Plane is active
Audit recent uploads for code or secret material

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while Plane does not advertise filesystem write. The main conflict is limited to shared files or local resources, not overlapping unrestricted writes or git mutation, so the blast radius is small and low fits better than medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local directory
IF Plane imports files that Continue is simultaneously editing
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent during bulk file imports
Use OS file locks on shared artifacts
Avoid concurrent edits to the same attachment set

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or task text from editor context, and Plane stores issues, tasks, and roadmaps that may be acted on later. If Plane treats Continue-produced text as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect tasking or planning; the interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Plane users copy Continue-generated summaries into issues without review
IF an MCP workflow sends Continue output directly into Plane tasks
mitigations: Require human review before creating Plane issues from AI text
Tag AI-generated content in task descriptions
Add a checklist for source verification
Limit Continue output to drafts, not final task records

E_compliance.rationale: Continue is an IDE assistant touching source code and editor buffers, while Plane is an issue/task system with files and notes. No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either profile, so only a low compliance concern remains from generic shared-data handling; the other agent is not separately cited because no specific cross-border or regulated-data claim is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Plane tasks or attachments
IF the same regulated dataset is also opened in Continue
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools unless approved
Use separate retention policies for task text and code
Document where attachments are stored
Review whether self-hosted Plane is required for sensitive projects
